agent_answer.notes: The corpus answers the question with a split result. Across the 52 papers that report a retrieval-augmented (RAG) system alongside a non-RAG baseline (parametric-only / vanilla / no-retrieval / closed-book) and a per-dataset latency figure, RAG increased latency in 25 papers (row r1), decreased it in 18 (row r2), and had a mixed or negligible dataset-dependent effect in 9 (row r3). There is no single consistent direction; whether RAG changes latency and in which direction depends on the specific system, dataset and retrieval configuration. Latency is measured in seconds as 'mean seconds needed to produce one answer'. S109 (a survey) notes that retrieval latency is reported in only a handful of papers and never together with the generation cost, so the empirical evidence comes from the main-comparison tables of the 52 papers listed. Paper ids are the corpus file names (S001..S112).
